final_candidates.decision_summary: K119 (verified as K in the supplied sequence) forms the covalent internal aldimine with PLP; removing this lysine eliminates cofactor anchoring and catalysis while leaving the overall fold essentially intact. This is the most mechanistically certain route to complete loss of activity.

G307 is verified in the catalytic domain; adding a side chain at this tightly packed conserved glycine causes misfolding/aggregation with essentially undetectable activity and no pyridoxine rescue. It is one of the best-characterized severe loss-of-function CBS substitutions.

T191 is verified adjacent to the PLP/catalytic core; substitution with a bulky Met disrupts the active-site environment and yields a severe, pyridoxine-non-responsive near-null phenotype. Slightly below G307S only because part of its effect is folding-mediated rather than strictly catalytic.

stop_reason.detail: Candidate pool converged and additional LLM-only rounds are unlikely to change the Top-3 ordering.

history.rationale: Lys119 forms the essential Schiff base with the pyridoxal-5'-phosphate cofactor in the CBS catalytic core; removing the ε-amino group eliminates internal aldimine formation and catalysis while leaving the fold largely intact.

Position 119 is K in the given sequence and is the PLP Schiff-base lysine; removing the covalent aldimine anchor is the most mechanistically certain route to complete loss of catalytic activity while the fold is largely preserved.

Gly307 lies in a tightly packed catalytic-domain turn where any side chain is sterically prohibited; the G307S substitution is the classic severe, pyridoxine-nonresponsive homocystinuria allele with essentially null activity.
G307 verified; introducing a beta-branched-adjacent side chain at a tightly packed catalytic-domain glycine causes misfolding/aggregation with near-zero activity and no pyridoxine rescue.

Thr191 sits in the PLP/substrate-binding region following the beta-strand after the TSGNT motif; the bulky Met substitution is a well-known severe loss-of-function allele causing misfolding and inactive enzyme.
T191 verified in sequence; this catalytic-core substitution is a classic severe, pyridoxine-non-responsive CBS lesion producing essentially null activity, so I raise it above G307S-level ties.

Arg336 makes buried salt-bridge/hydrogen-bond contacts stabilizing the catalytic core; loss of the charged guanidinium plus an unpaired cysteine is a documented severe, pyridoxine-nonresponsive inactivating change.
R336 verified; loss of a buried salt-bridge-forming arginine plus a free cysteine destabilizes the catalytic core, a documented severe LOF class.

Gly139 occupies a backbone-flexible position in the catalytic domain where introducing a large positive Arg causes steric/electrostatic disruption; reported as a severe inactivating homocystinuria mutation.
G139 verified; a large charged residue at a conserved backbone-flexible glycine near the catalytic domain should severely disrupt folding/activity.
Arg125 is adjacent to the PLP-binding lysine loop and anchors the cofactor phosphate environment; neutralizing it to Gln disrupts PLP positioning and yields near-null activity.
R125 verified and lies near the PLP-binding region; charge loss is a documented severe, non-responsive lesion, but folding-only effects keep it below the top tier.
Cys52 is one of the two axial ligands of the regulatory heme; substituting the thiolate destabilizes heme incorporation and folding, strongly compromising enzyme activity.
C52 is a heme axial ligand, but heme-ligand variants typically retain substantial (even near-normal) catalytic activity, so this poorly serves a strict abolish-activity objective.

rejection.reason: C52 is a heme axial ligand, but heme-ligand variants typically retain substantial (even near-normal) catalytic activity, so this poorly serves a strict abolish-activity objective.

history.rationale: His65 is the second axial heme ligand; replacement with Arg abolishes proper heme coordination, impairing folding and catalytic competence of the enzyme.
The other heme ligand; reported variants at this site retain considerable residual activity and are regulation-altering rather than null.

rejection.reason: The other heme ligand; reported variants at this site retain considerable residual activity and are regulation-altering rather than null.

history.rationale: Thr262 lies in the conserved GTGGT-adjacent catalytic region; the bulky Met substitution is a recognized pathogenic allele that severely reduces enzymatic activity.
T262 verified adjacent to the PLP-phosphate loop; bulky substitution is expected to strongly impair cofactor binding.

Asn228 contributes hydrogen bonding within the catalytic domain interface; the N228S change is a documented pathogenic variant with markedly reduced CBS activity, though some residual function may persist.
N228 verified, but this is a classic pyridoxine-responsive lesion with measurable residual activity, i.e., partial rather than abolished function.
